rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated phrase ‘before it’ emphasizes the long absence of rain and the people’s entrenched despair; its pronoun may refer to rain, clouds, or the sending of rain.
rows.anchor: تكرير للتأكيد والدلالة على تطاول عهدهم بالمطر واستحكام يأسهم، وقيل الضمير للمطر أو السحاب أو الإرسال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Despairing’ means having lost hope.
rows.anchor: وقيل الضمير للمطر أو السحاب أو الإرسال. { لمبلسين } لآيسين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The traces of mercy are rain’s effects in plants, trees, and many kinds of fruit.
rows.anchor: أثر الغيث من النبات والأشجار وأنواع الثمار

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: These readers recite ‘traces’ in the plural.
rows.anchor: ولذلك جمعه ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وحفص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate reading uses the feminine verb, assigning the act of reviving to ‘mercy.’
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالتاء على إسناده إلى ضمير الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one able to revive the earth after its death is able to revive the dead.
rows.anchor: لمحيي الموتى } لقادر على إحيائهم فإنه إحداث لمثل ما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Resurrection creates again the animal powers once present in bodily matter, just as reviving earth creates its former vegetal powers; bodily matter may include material dispersed in earlier years.
rows.anchor: فإنه إحداث لمثل ما كان في مواد أبدانهم من القوى الحيوانية، كما أن إحياء الأرض إحداث لمثل ما كان فيها من القوى النباتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can do every possible thing because all possible things stand equally in relation to His power.
rows.anchor: لأن نسبة قدرته إلى جميع الممكنات على سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Lost in the earth’ can mean becoming soil mixed indistinguishably with earth, or disappearing into it.
rows.anchor: أي صرنا ترابا مخلوط بتراب الأرض لا نتميز منه، أو غبنا فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read with kasra, from ḍalla yaḍillu, and with ṣād, from meat becoming putrid.
rows.anchor: وقرأ «ضللنا» بالكسر من ضل يضل «وصللنا } من صل اللحم إذا أنتن

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads ‘when’ as a declarative statement, governed by an implied meaning in the verse.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر «إذا» على الخبر والعامل فيه ما دل عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question means: will we be raised or have our creation renewed?
rows.anchor: وهو: نبعث أو يجدد خلقنا

rows.speaker: نافع والكسائي ويعقوب
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ, al-Kisāʾī, and Yaʿqūb read ‘that we are’ declaratively.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع والكسائي ويعقوب «أنا» على الخبر

rows.speaker: أبي بن خلف
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Khalaf is identified as the speaker; the statement is attributed to all because they accepted it.
rows.anchor: والقائل أبي بن خلف وإسناده إلى جميعهم لرضاهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of meeting their Lord means denying resurrection, or denying the encounter with the Angel of Death and what follows.
rows.anchor: بل هم بلقاء ربهم } بالبعث أو بتلقي ملك الموت وما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are deniers.
rows.anchor: أو بتلقي ملك الموت وما بعده. { كفرون } جاحدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Morning and evening are singled out for remembrance because they are especially excellent and witnessed, just as tasbīḥ is singled out among remembrances because it is their core.
rows.anchor: وتخصيصهما بالذكر للدلالة على فضلهما على سائر الأوقات لكونهما مشهودين كأفراد التسبيح من جملة الأذكار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view directs both verbs to morning and evening.
rows.anchor: وقيل الفعلان موجهان إليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view interprets tasbīḥ here as prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالتسبيح الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ṣalāt upon believers is mercy; the angels’ ṣalāt is asking forgiveness and attending to what benefits them.
rows.anchor: { هو الذى يصلي عليكم } بالرحمة. { وملئكته } بالاستغفار لكم والاهتمام بما يصلحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣalāt is used in its shared sense of attending to believers’ welfare and making their honor manifest, figuratively derived from ṣalw.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالصلاة المشترك وهو العناية بصلاح أمركم وظهور شرفكم مستعار من الصلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ṣalāt means mercy and spiritual inclination, drawn from the bodily inclination of bowing and prostration in prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل الترحم والانعطاف المعنوي مأخوذ من الصلاة المشتملة على الانعطاف الصوري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels’ supplication is mercy, especially because their prayers are answered and thereby cause mercy.
rows.anchor: واستغفار الملائكة ودعاؤهم للمؤمنين ترحم عليه سيما وهو السبب للرحمة من حيث إنهم مجابو الدعوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God brings believers from the darknesses of disbelief and sin into the lights of faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: من ظلمات الكفر والمعصية إلى نوري الإيمان والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is merciful to believers by tending to their welfare, raising their standing, and employing the angels closest to Him in this care.
rows.anchor: حيث اعتنى بصلاح أمرهم وإنافة قدرهم واستعمل في ذلك ملائكته المقربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan had no coercive power over them, only whispering and beguiling influence.
rows.anchor: تسلط واستيلاء بالوسوسة والاستغواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Except that We know’ means divine knowledge becomes related to the matter so that recompense follows, or that believers are distinguished from doubters, or that each follows his decreed faith or error; ‘knowledge’ emphatically stands for what it concerns.
rows.anchor: إلا ليتعلق علمنا بذلك تعلقا يترتب عليه الجزاء، أو ليتميز المؤمن من الشاك، أو ليؤمن من قدر إيمانه ويشك من قدر ضلاله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The matching forms of the two relative clauses have a subtle rhetorical point.
rows.anchor: في نظم الصلتين نكتة لا تخفى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord is a protector; the two forms are closely related.
rows.anchor: محافظ والزنتان متآخيتان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command addresses the idolaters and means the beings they claimed were gods; the two objects of ‘claim’ are elided in a specific way, with the relative clause lengthening the first and its attribute standing for the second.
rows.anchor: أي زعمتموهم آلهة، وهما مفعولا زعم حذف الأول لطول الموصول بصلته والثاني لقيام صفته مقامه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase cannot be treated as only the second object because the pronoun would not fit, nor can ‘they possess nothing’ be that object because the idolaters do not claim it.
rows.anchor: ولا يجوز أن يكون هو مفعوله الثاني لأنه لا يلتئم مع الضمير كلاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are challenged to invoke the claimed gods for benefit or harm, if their claim is true; the answer is supplied to forestall disputation.
rows.anchor: ادعوهم فيما يهمكم من جلب نفع أو دفع ضر لعلهم يستجيبون لكم إن صح دعواكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claimed deities possess not even an atom’s weight of good or evil anywhere in the heavens or earth.
rows.anchor: لا يملكون مثقال ذرة } من خير أو شر. { في السموات ولا فى الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Heavens and earth may mean all affairs in ordinary usage; alternatively, the deities include heavenly angels and stars and earthly idols, or the celestial and terrestrial proximate causes of good and evil.
rows.anchor: في أمر ما وذكرهما للعموم العرفي، أو لأن آلهتهم بعضها سماوية كالملائكة والكواكب وبعضها أرضية كالأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence independently explains their condition: they have no share in creation or ownership and no assistant in managing the two realms.
rows.anchor: لا خلقا ولا ملكا. { وما لهم منهم من ظهير } يعينه على تدبير أمرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels declare that only God is their patron and that they had no allegiance to the idolaters, disavowing approval of their worship.
rows.anchor: أنت الذي نواليه من دونهم لا موالاة بيننا وبينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The humans actually worshipped devils by obeying their commands to worship beings besides God.
rows.anchor: أي الشياطين حيث أطاعوهم في عبادة غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, devils appeared to the humans as angels and made them think they were angels, whom they then worshipped.
rows.anchor: وقيل كانوا يتمثلون لهم ويخيلون إليهم أنهم الملائكة فيعبدونهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first pronoun in ‘most of them’ refers to humans or polytheists; ‘most’ means all, and the second pronoun refers to jinn.
rows.anchor: الضمير الأول للإنس أو للمشركين، والأكثر بمعنى الكل والثاني ل { الجن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Judgment Day neither group can benefit or harm the other because that is the domain of recompense and God alone requites.
rows.anchor: إذ الأمر فيه كله له لأن الدار دار جزاء وهو المجازي وحده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to taste the Fire coordinates with the denial of mutual power and explains why that denial was introduced.
rows.anchor: عطف على { لا يملك } مبين للمقصود من تمهيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that warning makes no difference and they will not believe was explained earlier in al-Baqara.
rows.anchor: سبق في سورة «البقرة» تفسيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only warning that achieves the intended benefit reaches the one who follows the Qur’an through reflection and practice.
rows.anchor: إنذارا يترتب عليه البغية المرومة. { من اتبع الذكر } أي القرآن بالتأمل فيه والعمل به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fears the Merciful unseen by fearing punishment before it arrives and its terrors are seen, or by fearing inwardly without being deceived by mercy, since God is also avenging and overpowering.
rows.anchor: وخاف عقابه قبل حلوله ومعاينة أهواله، أو في سريرته ولا يغتر برحمته فإنه كما هو رحمن، منتقم قهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What they ask for’ may mean what they request for themselves, using a reflexive form, as in preparing roast or clarified butter for oneself.
rows.anchor: ما يدعون به لأنفسهم يفتعلون من الدعاء كاشتوى واجتمل إذا شوى وجمل لنفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it means what they ask one another for, as a reciprocal form like ‘they threw at one another.’
rows.anchor: أو ما يتداعونه كقولك ارتموه بمعنى تراموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it means what they wish for, from the idiom ‘ask me for anything’ meaning ‘wish it for me.’
rows.anchor: أو يتمنون من قولهم ادع علي ما شئت بمعنى تمنه علي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively it refers to what they sought in this world: Paradise and its degrees.
rows.anchor: أو ما يدعونه في الدنيا من الجنة ودرجاتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘What’ may be relative or indefinite; it is the subject and ‘for them’ its predicate.
rows.anchor: موصولة أو موصوفة مرتفعة بالابتداء، و { لهم } خبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Peace’ may be an appositive or further adjective, the predicate, a predicate with an omitted subject, or the subject of an omitted-predicate clause.
rows.anchor: سلم } بدل منها أو صفة أخرى، ويجوز أن يكون خبرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word may be read in the accusative as a verbal noun or circumstantial expression, meaning their wish is granted completely.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالنصب على المصدر أو الحال أي لهم مرادهم خالصا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting may be spoken by God or conveyed to them from Him; it honors them and fulfills their desire, and its accusative may mark specification.
rows.anchor: أي يقول الله أو يقال لهم قولا كائنا من جهته، والمعنى أن الله يسلم عليهم بواسطة الملائكة أو بغير واسطة تعظيما لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The criminals are separated from believers when the latter are led to Paradise, as in the verse about people separating when the Hour comes.
rows.anchor: وانفردوا عن المؤمنين وذلك حين يسار بهم إلى الجنة كقوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, criminals are separated from every good, or dispersed in Hell, each unbeliever isolated in a house where he neither sees nor is seen.
rows.anchor: وقيل اعتزلوا من كل خير أو تفرقوا في النار فإن لكل كافر بيتا ينفرد به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address reproaches the damned and establishes the proof; God’s covenant is the rational and transmitted evidence commanding His worship and forbidding worship of others.
rows.anchor: وعهده إليهم ما نصب لهم من الحجج العقلية والسمعية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worshipping Satan is named because Satan commands and adorns that worship.
rows.anchor: وجعلها عبادة الشيطان، لأنه الآمر بها والمزين لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is also read with a kasra on its imperfect prefix, as ‘aḥhad,’ or as ‘aḥad’ in the speech of Banū Tamīm.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { أعهد } بكسر حرف المضارعة و «أحهد» و «أحد» على لغة بني تميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan’s being an evident enemy explains why obedience to him is forbidden: he induces people to follow his commands.
rows.anchor: تعليل للمنع عن عبادته بالطاعة فيها يحملهم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to worship God is coordinated with the prohibition against worshipping Satan.
rows.anchor: عطف على { أن لا تعبدوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘This is a straight path’ points either to the covenant or to worshipping God; it explains the reason for the covenant, in both parts or only the second.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما عهد إليهم أو إلى عبادته، فالجملة استئناف لبيان المقتضي للعهد بشقيه أو بالشق الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite form magnifies the path, or is partitive because monotheism is one portion of the straight path.
rows.anchor: والتنكير للمبالغة والتعظيم، أو للتبعيض فإن التوحيد سلوك بعض الطريق المستقيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The resurrection will be one cry, the second blast; its name derives from a shepherd shouting to his flock, and its bringing forth is as effortless as ‘Be’ at the first creation.
rows.anchor: زجرة } أي صيحة واحدة، وهي النفخة الثانية من زجر الراعي غنمه إذا صاح عليها وأمرها في الإعادة كأمر { كن } في الإبداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the cry, people stand alive from their graves and see, or they await what will be done to them.
rows.anchor: فإذا هم قيام من مراقدهم أحياء يبصرون، أو ينتظرون ما يفعل بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call it the Day of Recompense, the day they are repaid for their deeds, and their speech ends there.
rows.anchor: اليوم الذي نجازى بأعمالنا وقد تم به كلامهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that this is the Day of Judgment is the angels’ answer; alternatively, some of the people say it to one another. Judgment means adjudication or distinguishing good-doers from wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: جواب الملائكة، وقيل هو أيضا من كلام بعضهم لبعض والفصل القضاء، أو الفرق بين المحسن والمسيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Gather the wrongdoers’ may be God’s order to the angels or an order among themselves to bring them from their place to the gathering, or to Hell.
rows.anchor: أمر الله للملائكة، أو أمر بعضهم لبعض بحشر الظلمة من مقامهم إلى الموقف. وقيل منه إلى الجحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their counterparts may be their like in idolatry, their wives who shared their religion, or their devil companions; the first view is compared with the three groups in 56:7.
rows.anchor: وأشباههم عابد الصنم مع عبدة الصنم وعابد الكوكب مع عبدته كقوله تعالى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deities they worshipped besides God are added to increase their regret and shame; the category is qualified by the exception of those promised the best reward, showing that the wrongdoers here are polytheists.
rows.anchor: زيادة في تحسيرهم وتخجيلهم، وهو عام مخصوص بقوله تعالى: { إن الذين سبقت لهم منا الحسنى } الآية، وفيه دليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Guide them to the path of Hell’ means show them a path they must travel.
rows.anchor: فعرفوهم طريقا ليسلكوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Repaid’ means recompensed, from dīn in the sense of requital.
rows.anchor: أءذا متنا وكنا ترابا وعظما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speaker asks whether his companions will look into Hell so he can show them his former companion.
rows.anchor: إلى أهل النار لأريكم ذلك القرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God or an angel asks whether they wish to view Hell’s inhabitants and see the companion, learning their own rank relative to his.
rows.anchor: وقيل القائل هو الله سبحانه وتعالى أو بعض الملائكة يقول لهم: هل تحبون أن تطلعوا على أهل النار لأريكم ذلك القرين

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr reads ‘you look, then I look’ with a lightened form, kasra on nūn, and ḍamma on the alif; their viewing prompts his, since companionship etiquette bars monopolizing the view.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي عمرو «مطلعون فأطلع» بالتخفيف وكسر النون وضم الألف على أنه جعل اطلاعهم سبب اطلاعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, he addresses angels using a connected pronoun in place of a separate one, as in the cited verse, or the active participle is made like a present verb.
rows.anchor: أو خاطب الملائكة على وضع المتصل موضع المنفصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided Moses and Aaron along the path that leads to truth and right judgment.
rows.anchor: الطريق الموصل إلى الحق والصواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the two were believing servants has been explained earlier in the same way.
rows.anchor: سبق مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elijah is among the messengers; he is Elijah son of Yāsīn, Aaron’s descendant and Moses’s brother, sent after Moses.
rows.anchor: هو إلياس بن ياسين سبط هرون أخى موسى بعث بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Elijah is Idrīs, since Idrīs and Idrās are read in its place and in Ubayy’s codex.
rows.anchor: وقيل إدريس لأنه قرىء إدريس وإدراس مكانه وفي حرف أبي رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another form is Īlīs; Ibn Dhakwān, with disagreement in transmission from him, omits the hamza in Ilyās.
rows.anchor: وقيل إيليس وقرأ ابن ذكوان مع خلاف عنه بحذف همزة إلياس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elijah called his people to fear God’s punishment.
rows.anchor: عذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Do you invoke Baal?’ can mean worship him or seek good from him; Baal was the idol of Baalbek in Syria, the city now called Baalbek.
rows.anchor: أتعبدونه أو أتطلبون الخير منه، وهو اسم صنم كان لأهل بك من الشام وهو البلد الذي يقال له الآن بعلبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, baʿl means ‘lord’ in Yemeni speech, so the question is whether they call on one of the lords.
rows.anchor: وقيل البعل الرب بلغة اليمن، والمعنى أتدعون بعض البعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the best of creators means abandoning His worship; the question first signals the reason for censure and then states it directly.
rows.anchor: أحسن الخلقين } وتتركون عبادته، وقد أشار فيه إلى المقتضي للإنكار المعني بالهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is exalted above what the polytheists attributed to Him in this sūra; ‘Lord of Might’ is ascribed to Him because might belongs only to Him or to whoever He empowers.
rows.anchor: عما قاله المشركون فيه على ما حكي في السورة، وإضافة الرب إلى العزة لاختصاصها به إذ لا عزة إلا له أو لمن أعزه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase encompasses God’s negative and positive attributes and signals oneness.
rows.anchor: وقد أدرج فيه جملة صفاته السلبية والثبوتية مع الإشعار بالتوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Peace is extended to all messengers after particular mention of some of them.
rows.anchor: تعميم للرسل بالتسليم بعد تخصيص بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Praise thanks God for blessings bestowed on the messengers and their followers and for the good end; it follows the greeting, teaching believers to praise Him and bless His messengers.
rows.anchor: على ما أفاض عليهم وعلى من اتبعهم من النعم وحسن العاقبة ولذلك أخره عن التسليم، والمراد تعليم المؤمنين كيف يحمدونه ويسلمون على رسله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī says that whoever wants the fullest measure of reward on Judgment Day should end his gathering with the closing words of this sūra.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه: من أحب أن يكتال بالمكيال الأوفى من الأجر يوم القيامة فليكن آخر كلامه من مجلسه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that reciting al-Ṣāffāt earns ten good deeds per jinn and devil, distances rebellious jinn and devils, clears the reciter of shirk, and brings testimony from the two guardians to faith; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: وعن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to worship God while making religion exclusively His, that is, affirming His oneness.
rows.anchor: موحدا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to be first among Muslims means precedence in this life and the next through sincerity, or being the first Qurayshite and first among their followers to submit to God.
rows.anchor: مقدمهم في الدنيا والآخرة، لأن قصب السبق في الدين بالإخلاص أو لأنه أول من أسلم وجهه لله من قريش ومن دان بدينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command is coordinated with the first but qualified by its cause; worship with sincerity also requires precedence in religion.
rows.anchor: والعطف لمغايرة الثاني الأول بتقييده بالعلة، والإشعار بأن العبادة المقرونة بالإخلاص وإن اقتضت لذاتها أن يؤمر بها فهي أيضا تقتضيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the lām is extra, and the command is to lead in sincerity and begin by practicing it when calling others to it.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تجعل اللام مزيدة كما في أردت لأن أفعل فيكون أمر بالتقدم في الإخلاص والبدء بنفسه في الدعاء إليه بعد الأمر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disobedience means abandoning sincerity and inclining toward their shirk and ostentation; the punishment is severe because the Day is great in what it contains.
rows.anchor: والرياء. { عذاب يوم عظيم } لعظمة ما فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who feared their Lord are hurried to the abode of honor; alternatively, their mounts are driven, since they arrive riding.
rows.anchor: إسراعا بهم إلى دار الكرامة، وقيل سيق مراكبهم إذ لا يذهب بهم إلا راكبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They arrive in groups ranked according to their honor and station.
rows.anchor: على تفاوت مراتبهم في الشرف وعلو الطبقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted answer to ‘when they reach it’ conveys indescribable honor; the gates open before their arrival, so they are not kept waiting.
rows.anchor: حذف جواب إذا للدلالة على أن لهم حينئذ من الكرامة والتعظيم ما لا يحيط به الوصف، وأن أبواب الجنة تفتح لهم قبل مجيئهم غير منتظرين

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kūfan readers recite ‘and its gates were opened’ with a lightened form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون «فتحت» بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gatekeepers’ greeting means no harm will befall them; ‘you are pure’ means cleansed of the stain of sins.
rows.anchor: لا يعتريكم بعد مكروه. { طبتم } طهرتم من دنس المعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The causal fāʾ makes their purity the reason for entering and remaining forever; this does not exclude a sinner entering by pardon after God purifies him.
rows.anchor: والفاء للدلالة على أن طيبهم سبب لدخولهم وخلودهم، وهو لا يمنع دخول العاصي بعفوه لأنه مطهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saved praise God for fulfilling His promise of resurrection and reward.
rows.anchor: صدقنا وعده } بالبعث والثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘He made us inherit the earth’ means, metaphorically, the place where they settled; inheritance is its transfer to them as recompense for their deeds or their freedom to dispose of it like heirs.
rows.anchor: يريدون المكان الذي استقروا فيه على الاستعارة، وإيراثها تمليكها مخلفة عليهم من أعمالهم أو تمكينهم من التصرف فيها تمكين الوارث فيما يرثه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each inhabitant may settle wherever desired in the spacious Garden; its immaterial ranks do not compete for space, and the excellent reward is Paradise.
rows.anchor: أي يتبوأ كل منا في أي مقام أراده من جنته الواسعة، مع أن في الجنة مقامات معنوية لا يتمانع واردوها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels encircle the Throne; ‘from around’ either has an extra min or marks the starting point of encircling.
rows.anchor: محدقين. { من حول العرش } أي حوله و { من } مزيدة أو لابتداء الحفوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels praise God while enjoying remembrance of His majesty and generosity; the highest rank and pleasure is absorption in the divine attributes.
rows.anchor: ذاكرين له بوصفي جلاله وإكرامه تلذذا به، وفيه إشعار بأن منتهى درجات العليين وأعلى لذائذهم هو الاستغراق في صفات الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Judgment among them means assigning some to Hell and some to Paradise, or assigning angels their stations according to their rank.
rows.anchor: أي بين الخلق بإدخال بعضهم النار وبعضهم الجنة، أو بين الملائكة بإقامتهم في منازلهم على حسب تفاضلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those praising God for the just judgment are the believers among those judged, or the angels, whose mention is omitted because they are known and honored.
rows.anchor: والقائلون هم المؤمنون من المقضي بينهم أو الملائكة وطي ذكرهم لتعينهم وتعظيمهم

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to promise that one who recites al-Zumar will retain hope on Judgment Day and receive the reward of the fearful; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet recited Banī Isrāʾīl and al-Zumar every night.
rows.anchor: عن عائشة رضي الله عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s word that was fulfilled means either His threat or His decree of punishment; the phrase that they are people of the Fire is apposition to ‘word,’ as whole or part, reading it as wording or meaning.
rows.anchor: وعيده أو قضاؤه بالعذاب. { على الذين كفروا } بكفرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Throne-bearers are the cherubim, the angels’ highest rank and the first created; bearing and surrounding the Throne metaphorically describe preserving and managing it, or signify closeness to God and status in carrying out His command.
rows.anchor: الكروبيون أعلى طبقات الملائكة وأولهم وجودا وحملهم إياه وحفيفهم حوله مجاز عن حفظهم وتدبيرهم له، أو كناية عن قربهم من ذي العرش ومكانتهم عنده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They glorify God with comprehensive praise of His majestic and generous attributes; tasbīḥ is primary and praise is their state because praise follows their condition whereas tasbīḥ is essential.
rows.anchor: يذكرون الله بمجامع الثناء من صفات الجلال والإكرام، وجعل التسبيح أصلا والحمد حالا لأن الحمد مقتضى حالهم دون التسبيح أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their faith is mentioned to honor faith and its people; the passage leads into their prayer for believers, and shows Throne-bearers and people on beds equal in knowing God, against anthropomorphists.
rows.anchor: أخبر عنهم بالإيمان إظهارا لفضله وتعظيما لأهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their forgiveness-seeking is their intercession, prompting repentance, or inspiring believers with what brings forgiveness; shared faith entails mutual counsel and compassion across kinds, as 49:10 says believers are brothers.
rows.anchor: واستغفارهم شفاعتهم وحملهم على التوبة وإلهامهم ما يوجب المغفرة، وفيه تنبيه على أن المشاركة في الإيمان توجب النصح والشفقة وإن تخالفت الأجناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Our Lord’ is what the angels say and either explains their seeking forgiveness or is circumstantial.
rows.anchor: أي يقولون { ربنا } وهو بيان ل { يستغفرون } أو حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording means God’s mercy and knowledge encompass everything; the phrasing intensifies their universality, and mercy comes first because it is the intended petition.
rows.anchor: أي وسعت رحمتك وعلمك فأزيل عن أصله للإغراق في وصفه بالرحمة والعلم والمبالغة في عمومها، وتقديم الرحمة لأنها المقصودة بالذات ها هنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask forgiveness for those known to repent and follow the path of truth, and explicitly ask that they be kept from Hell to stress its severity.
rows.anchor: { وقهم عذاب الجحيم } واحفظهم عنه وهو تصريح بعد إشعار للتأكيد والدلالة على شدة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Day people are exposed, they have left their graves, or are visible without cover, or their souls, deeds, and secrets are made manifest.
rows.anchor: خارجون من قبورهم أو ظاهرون لا يسترهم شيء أو ظاهرة نفوسهم لا تحجبهم غواشي الأبدان، أو أعمالهم وسرائرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing about their persons, deeds, or states is hidden from God; this confirms their exposure and removes worldly assumptions.
rows.anchor: من أعيانهم وأعمالهم وأحوالهم، وهو تقرير لقوله { هم برزون } وإزاحة لنحو ما يتوهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Whose is the kingdom today?’ narrates the question and answer, or states what the manifest disappearance of causes and intermediaries indicates; in reality it always testifies to God’s sole dominion.
rows.anchor: حكاية لما يسأل عنه في ذلك اليوم ولما يجاب به، أو لما دل عليه ظاهر الحال فيه من زوال الأسباب وارتفاع الوسائط، وأما حقيقة الحال فناطقة بذلك دائما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each soul is repaid for what it acquired: beliefs and actions form states that bring pleasure or pain, unnoticed in life amid distractions but perceived when resurrection removes them.
rows.anchor: النفوس تكتسب بالعقائد والأعمال هيئات توجب لذتها وأملها لكنها لا تشعر بها في الدنيا لعوائق تشغلها، فإذا قامت قيامتها زالت العوائق وأدركت لذاتها وألمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no injustice through reducing reward or increasing punishment.
rows.anchor: ينقص الثواب وزيادة العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s reckoning is swift because no matter distracts Him from another, so people promptly receive what they deserve.
rows.anchor: إذ لا يشغله شأن عن شأن فيصل إليهم ما يستحقونه سريعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two misleaders are devils of the jinn and human kinds who drove people to error and disobedience.
rows.anchor: يعني شيطاني النوعين الحاملين على الضلالة والعصيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they are Iblīs and Cain, who established unbelief and murder.
rows.anchor: وقيل هما إبليس وقابيل فإنهما سنا الكفر والقتل

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر ويعقوب وأبو بكر والسوسي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, Ibn ʿĀmir, Yaʿqūb, Abū Bakr, and al-Sūsī read ‘show us’ in a lightened form, like the lightened form of fa-khiḏ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر ويعقوب وأبو بكر والسوسي { أرنا } بالتخفيف كفخذ في فخذ

rows.speaker: الدوري
rows.claim: Al-Dūrī reads with an abbreviated kasra on the rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الدوري باختلاس كسرة الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting the misleaders beneath their feet means trampling them in revenge, or placing them in the lowest depth; ‘lowest’ can describe station or humiliation.
rows.anchor: ندوسهما انتقاما منهما، وقيل نجعلهما في الدرك الأسفل. { ليكونا من الأسفلين } مكانا أو ذلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their statement ‘our Lord is God’ acknowledges His lordship and affirms His oneness.
rows.anchor: اعترافا بربوبيته وإقرارا بوحدانيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They persist in works; ‘then’ marks the rank of practice after the confession that begins steadfastness, or the difficulty of steadfastness, which seldom follows confession. Reports from the rightly guided caliphs about steadfast faith, sincere work, and obligations are examples of its parts.
rows.anchor: في العمل و { ثم } لتراخيه عن الإقرار في الرتبة من حيث أنه مبدأ الاستقامة، أو لأنها عسر قلما تتبع الإقرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Angels descend to comfort them in whatever concerns them, or at death, or when they emerge from the grave.
rows.anchor: فيما يعن لهم بما يشرح صدورهم ويدفع عنهم الخوف والحزن، أو عند الموت أو الخروج من القبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Do not fear’ concerns what lies ahead; ‘do not grieve’ concerns what they left behind. The following particle may be a verbal noun, a lightened أن with omitted bāʾ, or explanatory.
rows.anchor: ما تقدمون عليه. { ولا تحزنوا } على ما خلفتم وأن مصدرية أو مخففة مقدرة بالباء أو مفسرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised Paradise had been promised to them in worldly life through the messengers.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا على لسان الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cannot escape the afflictions decreed for them on earth; they have no protector to guard them from these or helper to drive them away.
rows.anchor: فائتين ما قضى عليكم من المصائب. { وما لكم من دون الله من ولي } يحرصكم عنها. { ولا نصير } يدفعها عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ‘running ones’ are ships sailing in the sea like mountains.
rows.anchor: السفن الجارية. { فى البحر كالأعلم } كالجبال

rows.speaker: الخنساء
rows.claim: Al-Khansāʾ’s verse uses علم for a mountain-like landmark: Ṣakhr is a guide-post with fire on its summit.
rows.anchor:
قالت الخنساء:
وإن صخرا لتأتم الهداة به
كأنه علم في رأسه نار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wind is also read in the plural.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «الرياح»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God wills, the ships remain motionless on the sea’s surface.
rows.anchor: فيبقين ثوابت على ظهر البحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient and grateful are those who devote themselves and restrain themselves to contemplate God’s signs and favors, or every fully faithful believer, since faith is half patience and half gratitude.
rows.anchor: لكل من وكل همته وحبس نفسه على النظر في آيات الله والتفكر في آلائه، أو لكل مؤمن كامل الإيمان فإن الإيمان نصفان نصف صبر ونصف شكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Destroy them’ means drown them by sending a violent wind; the ships stand for their people, as the verse says ‘for what they earned.’
rows.anchor: أو يهلكهن بإرسال الريح العاصفة المغرقة، والمراد إهلاك أهلها لقوله تعالى: { بما كسبوا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase compresses the meaning ‘send the wind, then destroy some and save others by pardon’; the reading يعفو begins an independent clause.
rows.anchor: وأصله أو يرسلها فيوبقهن لأنه قسيم يسكن فاقتصر فيه على المقصود كما في قوله تعالى: { ويعف عن كثير }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God takes the Prophet before showing him their punishment, He will still avenge them in this world and the next.
rows.anchor: فإنا منهم منتقمون } بعذاب في الدنيا والآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The emphatic particle mā is extra, serving like the oath lām to draw in the emphatic nūn.
rows.anchor: و «ما» مزيدة مؤكدة بمنزلة لام القسم في استجلاب النون المؤكدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, if God wills to show the Prophet the promised punishment, they cannot escape Him.
rows.anchor: فإنا عليهم مقتدرون } لا يفوتوننا

rows.speaker: يعقوب برواية رويس
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb through Ruways reads ‘We show you’ and likewise ‘We take you’ with a silent nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب برواية رويس أو { نرينك } بإسكان النون وكذا { نذهبن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must hold firmly to the revealed verses and laws; the path is straight and has no bend.
rows.anchor: فاستمسك بالذي أوحى إليك } من الآيات والشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading makes ‘revealed’ active, with God as its subject.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «أوحى» على البناء للفاعل وهو الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revelation is an honor for the Prophet and his people, who will be asked about it and their fulfillment of its due.
rows.anchor: لشرف لك. { ولقومك وسوف تسئلون } أي عنه يوم القيامة وعن قيامكم بحقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Ask those We sent before you’ means ask their communities and religious scholars.
rows.anchor: أي واسأل أممهم وعلماء دينهم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير والكسائي
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and al-Kisāʾī read the hamza lightly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير والكسائي بتخفيف الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether God ordained worship of idols besides the Merciful; it invokes prophetic consensus on monotheism to show this teaching is no innovation warranting lies and hostility.
rows.anchor: هل حكمنا بعبادة الأوثان وهل جاءت في ملة من مللهم، والمراد به الاستشهاد بإجماع الأنبياء على التوحيد والدلالة على أنه ليس بدع ابتدعه فيكذب ويعادي له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call Moses ‘magician’ from stubbornness and stupidity, or because they called a learned expert a magician.
rows.anchor: نادوه بذلك في تلك الحال لشدة شكيمتهم وفرط حماقتهم، أو لأنهم كانوا يسمون العالم الماهر ساحرا

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the hāʾ in ‘O you’ with ḍamma.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر بضم الهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask him to pray to his Lord to remove the punishment; ‘by what He covenanted with you’ may refer to his prophecy, God’s answering his prayer, or God’s lifting punishment from the guided.
rows.anchor: فيكشف عنا العذاب. { بما عهد عندك } بعهده عندك من النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means ‘by the covenant you fulfilled,’ namely faith and obedience.
rows.anchor: أو { بما عهد عندك } فوفيت به وهو الإيمان والطاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their declaration ‘we will surely be guided’ is their pledge of guidance.
rows.anchor: إننا لمهتدون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once the punishment is removed, they immediately break their pledge to become guided.
rows.anchor: فاجئوا نكث عهدهم بالاهتداء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh called out personally or through a herald, in the assembly or among his people after the punishment was lifted, fearing some might believe.
rows.anchor: بنفسه أو بمناديه. { في قومه } في مجمعهم أو فيما بينهم بعد كشف العذاب عنهم مخافة أن يؤمن بعضهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rivers are Nile’s branches, chiefly four: the River of the King, Ṭūlūn, Damietta, and Tanīs.
rows.anchor: أنهار النيل ومعظمها أربعة أنهر: نهر الملك، ونهر طولون، ونهر دمياط، ونهر تنيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Flow beneath me’ means beneath his palace or authority, or in front of him in his gardens.
rows.anchor: تحت قصري أو أمري، أو بين يدي في جناني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waw either coordinates the rivers with the kingdom and ‘flow’ is their circumstantial clause, or it is a circumstantial waw introducing ‘these rivers’ as subject, with ‘flow’ as predicate.
rows.anchor: والواو إما عاطفة لهذه { الأنهر } على الملك و { تجرى } حال منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh challenges his people to see his claimed power and wealth.
rows.anchor: الأنهر } صفتها و { تجرى } خبرها. { أفلا تبصرون } ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s ownership of the heavens and earth generalizes His power after it was specified; falsifiers lose when the Hour comes, and ‘that day’ is appositional.
rows.anchor: تعميم للقدرة بعد تخصيصها. { ويوم تقوم الساعة يومئذ يخسر المبطلون } أي ويخسر يوم تقوم و { يومئذ } بدل منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every nation is gathered together, or kneels poised on its knees; another reading means sitting on fingertips in readiness.
rows.anchor: مجتمعة من الجثوة وهي الجماعة، أو باركة مستوفزة على الركب. وقرىء «جاذية» أي جالسة على أطراف الأصابع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each nation is summoned to its record, the page of its deeds; Yaʿqūb’s parsing makes ‘every’ appositional to the first phrase and ‘is summoned’ adjectival or a second object.
rows.anchor: صحيفة أعمالها. وقرأ يعقوب { كل } على أنه بدل من الأول وتدعى صفة أو مفعول ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Today you are recompensed for what you did’ is understood as spoken speech.
rows.anchor: محمول على القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record is called God’s book because He commanded the scribes to write deeds; it testifies truthfully without addition or omission, and ‘We copied’ means We ordered the angels to record their deeds.
rows.anchor: أضاف صحائف أعمالهم إلى نفسه لأنه أمر الكتبة أن يكتبوا فيها أعمالهم.. { ينطق عليكم بالحق } يشهد عليكم بما عملتم بلا زيادة ولا نقصان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All praise belongs to God, Lord of the heavens, earth, and worlds, since every blessing comes from Him and these realms indicate the perfection of His power.
rows.anchor: إذا لكل نعمة منه ودال على كمال قدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Majesty belongs to God because its effects appear throughout the heavens and earth; He is unconquerable and wise in His decrees, so people should praise, magnify, and obey Him.
rows.anchor: إذ ظهر فيها آثارها. { وهو العزيز } الذي لا يغلب. { الحكيم } فيما قدر وقضى فاحمدوه وكبروه وأطيعوا له

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that reciting Sūrat al-Jāthiya leads God to conceal a person’s nakedness and calm their terror on the Day of Reckoning; no grading is stated.
rows.anchor: عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
